title: How Belden and RUCKUS help you simplify network integration
summary: Belden and RUCKUS can help you simplify network integration and build converged networks across IT and OT, wired and wireless, and edge and cloud environments.
body_markdown:
Consider a new 4K camera installed on a plant floor to catch quality issues: Additional data from the camera can expose a network bandwidth constraint that wasn’t an issue with existing network-connected equipment. Before a[return on the new camera investment](https://www.belden.com/blog/want-to-maximize-network-roi) can be seen, decisions must be made about where to process video data and how to get information from the camera to the people and systems that need it.


In this case, the **video data needs to reach compute that can analyze it quickly** enough to support decisions about quality. (Reject the part or stop the line to investigate a recurring defect?) Depending on what the video reveals, findings may also need to be shared with other operational or business systems, such as production reporting software.


As camera data moves from the production line to other areas of the organization, prior decisions made about network bandwidth and processing determine how quickly those results become available and where they can be used.


Increasingly, intelligent automation—from[AMRs](https://www.belden.com/blog/connecting-amrs-agvs-in-your-warehouse-cellular-or-wifi) and[AGVs](https://www.belden.com/blog/Supporting-Mobile-Automation-with-Fast-Roaming-in-Automotive-Environments) to AI-enabled[predictive maintenance](https://www.belden.com/blog/why-predictive-maintenance-is-a-win-win-for-warehouses-and-oems) and safety—depends on connections across technologies that have been designed and managed independently:


- Wired and wireless connectivity
- IT and OT networks
- Edge and cloud resources


**But that’s where convergence comes in.** More applications and initiatives depend on data exchange across all these domains, which means they need to work together without compromising operations.
